## Upstream changes 6.73.0 -> 6.74.0

**Verdict:** SAFE TO APPLY — the notes list bug fixes and small UI/feature additions only, no breaking changes, and MySQL 8.4 (already pinned) remains the database this release expects.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes

### Variables
- none — no renamed, removed or newly required variables in the release notes, compose file, or .env.example

### Data and dependencies
- none introduced by this range. The compose file already pins `mysql:8.4-oracle`, consistent with what Ghost has required at the current version (6.73.0) and continues to require at 6.74.0; this is a pre-existing fact, not a change in this upgrade.
- Image diff confirms only the expected version bump: `GHOST_VERSION`: '6.73.0' -> '6.74.0', plus internal `GHOST_CLI_VERSION`/`GHOST_CLI_SHA` bumps. No change to user, entrypoint, command, ports, volumes, healthcheck or environment shape between the two images.

### Before applying
- None required beyond the normal routine. As always with any Ghost upgrade, a database backup before applying is good practice — the `backups` service in this compose file already runs on a schedule (`BACKUP_INTERVAL`, default 24h); confirm a recent one exists before pulling the new image tag.

### Notes read
- TryGhost/Ghost release notes for v6.74.0 (upgrade target) and v6.73.0 (baseline, the version currently running), both quoted above. No UPGRADING / BREAKING_CHANGES / CHANGELOG section was supplied for this range.

## Upstream changes 11.0.1 -> 11.1.0

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — this release adds an account-lockout security feature and removes trusted CA roots, either of which can lock out admins or break outgoing HTTPS unexpectedly; no companion-service version is newly required.

### Breaking changes
- Local-account login lockout is now enforced after repeated failures: *"After five failed attempts, each within 15 minutes of the previous one, an account is now locked for ten minutes, and the login form explains when it can be tried again."* An admin who mistypes a password repeatedly (including via scripted/API logins) will be locked out for 10 minutes; recoverable with the new `occ user:unlock`, but this is new, active-by-default behaviour. (`#41805`)
- The CA bundle shipped in the image was replaced with a newer Mozilla extract, dropping 35 roots including several widely used ones: *"The removed roots include DigiCert Global Root CA, DigiCert Assured ID Root CA, DigiCert High Assurance EV Root CA, the Entrust root CAs, emSign Root CA - C1, emSign ECC Root CA - C3, COMODO Certification Authority and QuoVadis Root CA 2 and 3. Outgoing HTTPS connections to servers whose certificates chain only to a removed root now fail verification."* This can break external storage backends, federation, or webhook/notification targets that still chain to one of these roots. Fix via `occ security:certificates:import` if needed. (`#41908`)
- Stricter app-signature verification on install/update: *"The installer now verifies the signature of every app package it installs or updates... An app archive must contain exactly one app folder, named after the app id in its info.xml."* Unsigned third-party or custom-packaged apps may fail to install/update unless explicitly allow-listed via `integrity.ignore.missing.app.signature`. (`#41955`)

### Variables
- None renamed or removed in the compose file or `.env.example`.
- Optional new config knobs introduced by the application itself (not compose/.env variables): `account_lockout.*` PHP config parameters, for tuning the new lockout thresholds. Not present in `.env.example`; would need to be added to ownCloud's own `config.php` by hand if an operator wants to change the defaults.

### Data and dependencies
- None found regarding database/cache engine version requirements in this range. The compose file already pins `mariadb: 11.4` and `redis: 7.4`; the notes for this range name no different requirement for either.
- Certificate bundles are regenerated automatically on upgrade: *"The system certificate bundle and the user certificate bundles found in the data directory are now regenerated during occ upgrade and occ maintenance:repair."* This happens as part of the normal upgrade process, no manual step required, but see the CA-removal breaking change above for its effect.

### Before applying
- Take the usual backup before upgrading (the compose file's `backups` service already covers this; confirm a recent successful dump exists).
- After upgrading, check whether any external storage, federation peer, or outbound integration (e.g. object storage, SMTP, webhook endpoint) presents a certificate chaining only to one of the removed roots (DigiCert Global Root CA, DigiCert Assured ID Root CA, DigiCert High Assurance EV Root CA, Entrust roots, emSign Root CA - C1, emSign ECC Root CA - C3, COMODO Certification Authority, QuoVadis Root CA 2/3). If so, import it with `occ security:certificates:import` before or immediately after the upgrade.
- If any automation logs into ownCloud with a password and might retry on failure (health checks, scripts, CI), review it against the new 5-attempts/15-minute lockout window, or be ready to run `occ user:unlock <login>`.
- If any apps were installed outside the official signed channel, verify they still pass `occ integrity:check-app` or add them to `integrity.ignore.missing.app.signature`.

### Notes read
- `CHANGELOG.md` sections "Changelog for ownCloud Core [11.1.0] (2026-11-02)" (the version being moved to) and "Changelog for ownCloud Core [11.0.1] (2026-09-25)" (THE RELEASE THE TEMPLATE RUNS NOW, read only as baseline, not as a change in this range).
- The dedicated per-tag release notes (`v11.1.0`, `v10.16.7`, `v10.16.6`) were empty/content-free; the changelog file was used instead as the authoritative source for this range.
